problem: Prior VLN agents based on greedy local action selection cannot recover from wrong decisions and lack global comparison of partial trajectories against the instruction, which limits success rate and path efficiency.
motivation: VLN requires aligning panoramic visual input with natural language instructions in real time. Greedy step-wise decoding makes errors irreversible, while beam-search style approaches make paths long. A search that can backtrack while scoring partial paths against instructions could improve success rate and path length.
key_idea: Use a transformer-based joint multimodal embedding with multimodal and temporal context, plus a backtracking-enabled greedy local search (BGLS) that combines local action scores with a global score comparing the partial trajectory to multiple instructions.
insight: Only the abstract was available, so no ablation evidence can be cited. The abstract claims that combining local and global scores with backtracking improves success rate and path optimality relative to greedy decoding.
method: Joint multimodal embedding: a transformer-based module jointly encodes panoramic visual features and instruction language.
Multimodal and temporal context: the agent uses both cross-modal context and history of past steps for state representation.
BGLS: a greedy local search with a backtracking feature that returns to earlier candidate nodes when the current path looks wrong.
Local and global scoring: candidate actions are ranked with local scores and global scores of the partial trajectory.
Global scoring against multiple instructions: the trajectory searched so far is compared with a plurality of natural language instructions.
